raw_response:
I farm a small, irrigated wheat-maize rotation in Quzhou County, so I will keep the whole 4.1 mu in the same double-cropping system this year. On land this small, I value stable output and labor efficiency more than experimentation, especially since some family labor is tied up off-farm. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want dependable establishment, good yield, and stronger stress tolerance under local conditions. I will fertilize wheat a bit more heavily overall because it needs a solid base and spring support, while maize will get higher nitrogen to push vegetative growth and grain fill. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate enough to avoid obvious moisture stress but not excessively, because water and power still cost money. I will rely on rotary tillage because it is fast and practical for my scale. I will keep pesticide use moderate, applying only enough to protect yield in a normal year. My goal is steady, realistic production rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
